content.user_title: Build Azure AI Search Apps in TypeScript
content.value_statement: TypeScript developers need clear Azure AI Search patterns for modern retrieval features. This skill provides focused examples for indexes, vectors, hybrid search, semantic ranking, and document operations.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation commands for Azure Search Documents and Azure Identity packages.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential with SearchClient and SearchIndexClient.
Provides TypeScript examples for vector, hybrid, and semantic search.
Covers filters, facets, autocomplete, suggestions, and batch document operations.
Lists key Azure Search SDK types and practical search best practices.
limitations: Does not create Azure resources or validate service permissions.
Uses example schemas and documents that need production review.
Requires an existing Azure AI Search service and configured credentials.
Does not provide custom embedding generation implementation details.

use_cases.title: Create Search Indexes
use_cases.description: Plan a TypeScript index schema with searchable fields, filters, facets, and vector fields.

use_cases.title: Add Retrieval Features
use_cases.description: Implement full text, vector, hybrid, and semantic search patterns for application queries.

use_cases.title: Manage Search Documents
use_cases.description: Upload, merge, delete, and incrementally update indexed documents using batch operations.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Basic Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, explain the basic Azure AI Search TypeScript setup for a new project.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Index Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, design an Azure AI Search index for products with text, filters, facets, and vector fields.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Query Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, compare full text, vector, hybrid, and semantic search for my TypeScript application.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Indexing
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, create a production plan for batch indexing, incremental updates, filters, facets, and query performance monitoring.

output_examples.input: Design an Azure AI Search index for a product catalog.
output: A recommended field model with identifier, title, description, category, and embedding fields.
A vector profile plan using HNSW and a named search profile.
Notes on which fields should be searchable, filterable, and facetable.

output_examples.input: Help me choose between vector, hybrid, and semantic search.
output: A concise comparison of each query pattern and when to use it.
A recommended approach for natural language product discovery.
Configuration notes for semantic captions and extractive answers.

output_examples.input: Plan document updates for an existing search index.
output: A batch operation strategy for uploads, merges, and deletes.
Guidance to use incremental updates for changed documents.
Operational notes about monitoring query performance and counts.

best_practices: Use hybrid search when both keyword precision and semantic similarity matter.
Define filters and facets during schema design, not after launch.
Batch document changes and monitor expensive query options in production.
anti_patterns: Do not store secrets directly in prompts, examples, or source files.
Do not use vector search without matching embedding dimensions.
Do not rely on sample schemas without validating production access rules.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build TypeScript applications that use Azure AI Search indexes, documents, and query features.

faq.question: Does it support vector search?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes vector field setup and vector query examples for Azure AI Search.

faq.question: Does it cover semantic search?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows semantic configuration, semantic query options, captions, and extractive answers.

faq.question: Can it manage documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers uploads, batch operations, merge operations, delete actions, and incremental updates.

faq.question: Does it create Azure credentials?
faq.answer: No. You must provide Azure credentials and service permissions in your own environment.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
